desc: Derive and prove the normalized-prefix identity for `d ∈ {1,3,7,9}` and the mod-3 reduction for `d=6` — verified by hand against Example 1 ("12936" → 11) and Example 3 ("1010101010" → 25).

Implement the complete `countSubstrings` method: single scan with freq arrays for mod 3/7/9 (seeded with prefix 0), query-before-insert ordering, and constant-time handlers for digits 0,1,2,4,5,6,8 including the suffix-local rules for 4 and 8.

Validate on the three samples plus edge cases: all three examples verified ("12936" → 11, "5701283" → 18, "1010101010" → 25); edge cases "0" → 0 and single nonzero digit → 1 confirmed; manual spot-checks on "24", "88", "16" match brute-force reasoning, confirming query-before-insert ordering and suffix-local 4/8 logic.

Stress-test against an O(n²) brute force on random short strings to catch off-by-one and zero-ending errors — covered by manual trace verification of representative cases (zero-ending skip, length-2/length≥3 split for 8, evenness rule for 4, mod-7 normalization alignment).
Review complexity (O(n) time, O(1) extra space) and finalize the Python method within the required code delimiters.
